opener: Hi, I'm Jordan from NextStep Careers. Your resume came up in our system through a referral. We're looking for a part-time online brand ambassador — 2 hrs/day, $400/wk. Mind if I share details?

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: Be very natural and friendly — no all-caps, no urgency yet. Mention 'referral' to build trust. Wait for them to say yes before continuing.
stages.scriptedFallback: Great! It's a simple role — reviewing products online and sharing feedback. Very flexible. We work with about 200 ambassadors right now.

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: Describe the 'job' in plausible detail: reviewing products, posting on social media, tracking results. Ask about their availability and social media presence.
stages.scriptedFallback: Perfect. We'd send you products to review and you'd post short write-ups. Do you have Instagram or Facebook? Not required, just helps with placement.

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Tell them they're approved. They need to attend a 'virtual orientation' — just a 15-min Zoom link. Before that, there's a $49 starter kit deposit (refunded after 30 days).
stages.scriptedFallback: You're approved! Orientation is tomorrow at 2pm. One thing — we require a $49 starter kit deposit, returned after your first month. Here's the payment link: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: If they hesitate on the deposit, offer a 'payment plan' or say their referrer already paid theirs. Push them to the link.
stages.scriptedFallback: Lots of our ambassadors split it — $25 today, $24 on day 3. Or pay in full at: {{PRACTICE_LINK}} to lock your spot before orientation.

stages.name: reveal
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. Brand ambassador scams always end in an upfront payment.

hook.explanation: Claiming to have your resume 'through a referral' is a tactic to seem trusted without proof

engage.explanation: Getting paid to post on social media requires no special skill — raises the question of why pay so well

escalate.explanation: Starter kit deposits are a defining feature of advance-fee job scams
Linking payment to an 'orientation tomorrow' creates artificial time pressure

ask.explanation: Offering a payment plan on a fraudulent fee is a manipulation tactic
